question: Does a weak magnetic field at one end of a Hubbard chain induce the correct spin pattern throughout the chain?

model.ensemble: Zero-temperature fixed total particle number; all seven spin sectors checked

methods.target: User Hubbard MPO with ITensorMPS optimizer and new boundary-field/state-export validation adapters
independent_references: TeNPy FermiHubbardModel with independently constructed boundary field and DMRG
QuSpin complete independent exact eigensystems in all fixed-particle spin sectors
methods.attribution: ITensorMPS and TeNPy supply their respective optimizers. Field/export/contraction/certificate adapters are new validation code.

scope_limits: One finite-cluster ground-state response question, not thermodynamic magnetism or whole-package reliability.
Seven field values, two truncation arms and two initial states are coverage of P17, not additional benchmark ideas.
Uncertainty budgets are conditional floating arithmetic, not directed-rounding interval arithmetic.
Saved receipt auditing checks recorded relationships and source/runtime identity; it does not independently repeat all Hamiltonian/tensor/eigensystem calculations.
Original signed subtractive variances remain unchanged diagnostics. Positive H-residual squared is separate.
TeNPy uses its source-defined hybrid local diagonalization policy; no claim of uniform Lanczos updates.
Timings document verification work and do not establish a production-solver speedup.
All earlier failed or unresolved attempts remain recorded.
